question.text: Mr. Vikram Rao, Head of Distribution at 'Satpura AIF', is approached by a prospective LP who asks about 'pass-back' arrangements to sweeten subscriptions. Under SEBI (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations, 2003, which of the following is TRUE?

answer.text: Pass-backs (indirect incentives to induce subscriptions) and Soft-Dollar arrangements with distributors are prohibited; assuring returns is also prohibited. AIFs and distributors must observe high standards of ethics, integrity and fairness
Pass-backs are permitted if disclosed in the PPM and capped at 1% of subscription amount
Pass-backs are permitted only to Accredited Investors
Soft-Dollar arrangements are permitted because they reduce the fund's research cost

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 4 of SEBI (PFUTP) Regulations, 2003: AIFs and distributors cannot indulge in manipulative/fraudulent/unfair practices. Pass-backs are indirect incentives that create conflict of interest — they discourage merit-based investor decisions. Soft-Dollar arrangements (using client money to pay for research that aids firm management) are prohibited — research must be paid from the Manager's own assets unless it directly aids investment decision-making. Assuring returns is also prohibited. The Trap: Options A, C and D all try to legitimize practices that SEBI treats as per-se impermissible. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B test pass-back prohibition at the selling level. XIX-C tests the Manager-side obligation including Soft-Dollar and return-assurance. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: Insert 'No Pass-Back / No Soft-Dollar' covenants into the Distribution Agreement with placement agents. Train sales staff annually and track attestations. If a distributor offers a pass-back off-book, PFUTP violation attaches to the AIF Manager as well — joint-and-several liability risk.
